nodes_source.node_name: Data used to support the results of this study
nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic video data and empirical data used to calibrate simulation parameters for the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, China.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The Data Availability section explicitly states the dataset is available from the corresponding author upon request, but provides no public URL or DOI.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Simulation modeled a real-world freeway merge in SUMO. The road has three mainline lanes reducing to three after the one-lane ramp. Simulated period runs from 7:50 am to 9:00 am based on empirical flow volumes.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, tool specified precisely (though without specific version), critical physical modelling bounds strictly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed as the observation input of each decision time step.
nodes_process.description: The raw video state is transformed into an environmental matrix mapping spatial layout and phase. Images are zoomed, downsampled to 4x512 arrays, and temporally stacked by taking 3 consecutive decision interval samples to maintain vehicular dynamic info.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, input matrices shape explicit but zooming and spatial masking not reproducible mathematically since frame crop algorithms omit toolings.

nodes_process.source_quote: While training the ramp metering Q-network, the mean speed in the merging area and the queue length at the on-ramp are predicted simultaneously.
nodes_process.description: A CNN acts as a shared feature representation layer branching into multi-task heads for learning efficiency. Includes 3 conv layers, followed by parallel fully-connected dual units projecting predicted values for phase Q, speed and queue.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, network structures parameterised totally in fig7 although tool (tf/pytorch) relies on arbitrary convention.

nodes_process.source_quote: The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update w_i to minimize the loss function.
nodes_process.description: Training uses e-greedy logic updating parameters for stability via an offline fixed replay buffer combined with an asynchronously frozen target tracking network, executed iteratively up to converging bounds on computing node.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, optimization pseudo-code logic fully documented, every tabular parameter directly filled natively, tool specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on... downstream occupancies
nodes_process.description: Sets parameters for analytical comparison baseline algorithms incorporating unregulated fixed-phasing or no metering flow combined with PI-Alinea responsive gating configurations utilizing finely adjusted set parameters resolving local queue delays optimally.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, baseline control method structurally provided fully via constants tuning though tooling remains abstract simulation coding.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: Randomized multiple rollout sessions compute distribution characteristics over time, yielding mean speed mappings, flow tracking charts, distribution ranges of throughput queue limits testing the robustness vs purely algorithmic analytical counterparts.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, repeated experimental metrics evaluation details specified nicely but without strict randomizer initialization values rendering complete variance equality infeasible.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: Input spaces mapped natively into blocks were intentionally deactivated via feature replacement zeroing values one section systematically, isolating each location quadrant's signal capability for retaining the operational optimal efficiency.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, coordinate matrices for bounding ablation squares were solely pictured and undefined strictly; masking zeroing methodology presumed partially absent parameter tracking info.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time during training of the DRL agent over 1e6 frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Model setup and simulator (SUMO) parameterized clearly. Data requires request to access empirical inputs, hindering precise reproduction. Plausible simulation outcomes cleanly presented.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Plots showing quartiles (25%, 50%, 75%) of mainline travel times over time for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly supported by simulation results; methodology details mostly adequate, but inaccessible private traffic data sets strict reproducibility ceiling.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparative table summarizing the mean travel time in seconds for 20 independent SUMO simulation experiments under three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulations generated by explicit seeds; standard output aggregation. Missing empirical dataset acts as bottleneck.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps displaying temporal-spatial distribution of mean vehicular speed for the no control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL control schemes.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly aggregates vehicle speed matrices. Supported well. Needs raw data inputs to reproduce exact speeds shown.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series band chart depicting queue lengths distributions (Q1, Q2, Q3) spanning three control algorithms over one hour.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Well-formatted extraction of queue traces, clearly justified claims, although raw input data must be available to recalculate.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios [...] in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots highlighting the relationship between queue lengths and signal red-ratios for PI-ALINEA and Deep RL approaches.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plots extracted attributes directly output by SUMO logs under standard setup, bottleneck remains the closed case-study empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Dual line chart showing downstream mainline occupancy (%) overplotted with on-ramp queue length (m) for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) Deep RL methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear variables and aggregation logic, firmly aligned with statements; upstream dataset needed for direct generation.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Grouped boxplots presenting 5-minute aggregation buckets of vehicle flow downstream under three evaluated operational approaches.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Valid empirical presentation logically matching claim. Dependent entirely upon SUMO model simulation results configured via non-public real-world traffic data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Boxplot comparing the travel times between a robustly run unperturbed DRL instance against eight perturbing settings disabling subsets of positional information.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Method conceptually established (zeroing pixel inputs subarea by subarea); claim supports network robustness but suffers reproducibility limits from inaccessible initial scenario matrices.
